title: SpREM: Exploiting Hamming Sparsity for Fast Quantum Readout Error Mitigation
problem: Quantum readout error severely reduces measurement fidelity in NISQ devices. Matrix-based error mitigation suffers from poor scalability and limited fidelity improvement as the mitigation matrix size grows exponentially with the number of qubits.
motivation: High quantum readout error in current NISQ systems limits measurement accuracy, and existing matrix-based error mitigation techniques lack sufficient scalability for practical quantum computation.
method: SpREM identifies patterns in the error matrix using Hamming distance (a measure of how different two values are) to pinpoint which qubits interact and affect each other's measurement errors. It then compresses the matrix using the Hamming-Distance Sparse Row (HDSR) method, removing parts that don't matter more effectively than threshold-based pruning that just discards small numbers. This compressed matrix is then implemented on hardware to quickly correct quantum readout errors.
key_novelty: The core idea is using Hamming distance (counting how many bits differ between values) to find patterns in quantum error matrices that enable more effective compression and higher measurement accuracy than simply discarding small values.
contributions: Novel identification of structured sparsity in error mitigation matrices using Hamming distance based on qubit interactions
HDSR compression method achieving 98.9% sparsity with 27.3× reduction in fidelity loss compared to threshold-based pruning
Hardware-efficient computational dataflow design for HDSR format
11.2×-36.4× speedup over Xilinx Vitis SPARSE and NVIDIA A100 GPU implementations

metrics.speedup: 11.2×-36.4× vs Vitis SPARSE and A100 GPU

limitations: Applicability to different quantum processor architectures and scalability to larger numbers of qubits are not discussed.
